problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨12(1+2t)^{3},9(1-3t)^{2}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨1,6⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Velocity Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration

feedback.problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,{e}^{t}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨5,\,e⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the components of the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=4.$ Do not round the answers.

$v(4)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},{e}^{t}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,\text{d}t,\int {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{t}+{C}_{1},\,{e}^{t}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨5,e⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨\sqrt{1}+{C}_{1},\,{e}^{1}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨5,e⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},\,e+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have ${C}_{1}=4$ and ${C}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the velocity is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨\sqrt{t}+4,\,{e}^{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity at time $t=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(4) & =⟨\sqrt{4}+4,\,{e}^{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,{e}^{4}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
